The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including trafficking in persons has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general in nature, having no relevance to level of education, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and belief, as well as particular ethnicity, ethnic group, or race. One of the causes among others is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and trafficking in persons that has occurred so far is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and the Indonesian Child Prevention Network (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, the Regional Government also has the obligation and responsibility to prevent and sanction acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, healing and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus it is expected that the main objective of the preparation of this Draft Regional Regulation can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal basis for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons and to ensure the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and combating violence and trafficking.

Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within a country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Article 9

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency. 5. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within a country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance. 32. CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency. 5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within a country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Rights of the child are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or to a person's body, miscarriage and fainting and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers working abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery. 15. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and obscenity. 17. Recruitment is an act that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community. 18. Transfer is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. Debt bondage is the act of placing a person in the status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people under their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment. 20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination. 22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred. 23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in an effort to strengthen the victim psychologically. 25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as KPPA is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics. 26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process. 27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved. 29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance. 32. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter referred to as SPO is a procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree. 33.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including trafficking in persons has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general in nature, having no relevance to level of education, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and belief, as well as particular ethnicity, ethnic group, or race. One of the causes among others is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and trafficking in persons that has occurred so far is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and the Indonesian Child Prevention Network (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, the Regional Government also has the obligation and responsibility to prevent and sanction acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, healing and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus it is expected that the main objective of the preparation of this Draft Regional Regulation can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal basis for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons and to ensure the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and combating violence and trafficking.

CONCERNING

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD. REGENT OF BANYUWANGI,

Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general in nature, having no relevance to level of education, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and belief, as well as particular ethnicity, ethnic group, or race. One of the causes among others is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and trafficking in persons that has occurred so far is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and the Indonesian Child Prevention Network (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, the Regional Government also has the obligation and responsibility to prevent and sanction acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, healing and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus it is expected that the main objective of the preparation of this Draft Regional Regulation can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal basis for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons and to ensure the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and combating violence and trafficking.

2. The preparation of planning and budget documents as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be harmonized among related Regional Work Units (SKPD).

The SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection together with P2TP2A facilitates the integration of policies, programs, and activities for empowerment, protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons into the preparation of planning and budget documents as set forth in paragraph (1).

CHAPTER I

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency. 5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within a country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Rights of the child are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or to a person's body, miscarriage and fainting and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers working abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery. 15. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and obscenity. 17. Recruitment is an act that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community. 18. Transfer is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. Debt bondage is the act of placing a person in the status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people under their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment. 20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination. 22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred. 23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in an effort to strengthen the victim psychologically. 25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as KPPA is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics. 26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process. 27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved. 29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance. 32. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter referred to as SPO is a procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree. 33.

Discrimination against women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women; 34. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms. 35. Community institution is an institution formed by members of the Indonesian citizen community voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations. 36. Companion institution is an institution that provides assistance to women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons in Banyuwangi Regency. 37. Empathy is a mental condition that makes a person feel themselves to be in the same state of feeling or thought as the person or group who is a victim of violence and trafficking in persons.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE AND TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD. REGENT OF BANYUWANGI,

Considering:

a. that violence against women and children as well as trafficking in persons constitutes an act of degrading human dignity and degree, therefore they need to be provided with adequate services and protection; b. that the level of trafficking in persons, violence against women and children is still high, therefore it is the obligation of the regional government to regulate and serve the interests of the community, in this case women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons; c. that in order for the handling of trafficking in persons, violence against women and children to be implemented effectively and efficiently, it is necessary to regulate the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letters a, b and c, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons. I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including trafficking in persons has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general in nature, having no relevance to level of education, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and belief, as well as particular ethnicity, ethnic group, or race. One of the causes among others is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and trafficking in persons that has occurred so far is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and the Indonesian Child Prevention Network (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, the Regional Government also has the obligation and responsibility to prevent and sanction acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, healing and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus it is expected that the main objective of the preparation of this Draft Regional Regulation can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal basis for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons and to ensure the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and combating violence and trafficking.

NUMBER 1 OF 2011

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE AND TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD. REGENT OF BANYUWANGI,

Considering:

a. that violence against women and children as well as trafficking in persons constitutes an act of degrading human dignity and degree, therefore they need to be provided with adequate services and protection; b. that the level of trafficking in persons, violence against women and children is still high, therefore it is the obligation of the regional government to regulate and serve the interests of the community, in this case women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons; c. that in order for the handling of trafficking in persons, violence against women and children to be implemented effectively and efficiently, it is necessary to regulate the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letters a, b and c, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons. I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including trafficking in persons has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general in nature, having no relevance to level of education, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and belief, as well as particular ethnicity, ethnic group, or race. One of the causes among others is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and trafficking in persons that has occurred so far is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and the Indonesian Child Prevention Network (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, the Regional Government also has the obligation and responsibility to prevent and sanction acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, healing and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus it is expected that the main objective of the preparation of this Draft Regional Regulation can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal basis for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons and to ensure the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and combating violence and trafficking.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including trafficking in persons has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general in nature, having no relevance to level of education, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and belief, as well as particular ethnicity, ethnic group, or race. One of the causes among others is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and trafficking in persons that has occurred so far is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and the Indonesian Child Prevention Network (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, the Regional Government also has the obligation and responsibility to prevent and sanction acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, healing and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus it is expected that the main objective of the preparation of this Draft Regional Regulation can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal basis for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons and to ensure the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and combating violence and trafficking.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency. 5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within a country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Rights of the child are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or to a person's body, miscarriage and fainting and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers working abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery. 15. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and obscenity. 17. Recruitment is an act that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community. 18. Transfer is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. Debt bondage is the act of placing a person in the status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people under their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment. 20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination. 22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred. 23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in an effort to strengthen the victim psychologically. 25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as KPPA is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics. 26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process. 27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved. 29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers working abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery. 15. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and obscenity. 17. Recruitment is an act that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community. 18. Transfer is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. Debt bondage is the act of placing a person in the status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people under their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment. 20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination. 22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred. 23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in an effort to strengthen the victim psychologically. 25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as KPPA is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics. 26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process. 27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved. 29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance. 32. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter referred to as SPO is a procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree. 33.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including trafficking in persons has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general in nature, having no relevance to level of education, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and belief, as well as particular ethnicity, ethnic group, or race. One of the causes among others is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and trafficking in persons that has occurred so far is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and the Indonesian Child Prevention Network (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, the Regional Government also has the obligation and responsibility to prevent and sanction acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, healing and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus it is expected that the main objective of the preparation of this Draft Regional Regulation can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal basis for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons and to ensure the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and combating violence and trafficking.

a. encourage victims to provide information to the authorities and be willing to become witnesses;
b. facilitate victims to be involved in efforts to prevent additional victims together with the community.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including trafficking in persons has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general in nature, having no relevance to level of education, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and belief, as well as particular ethnicity, ethnic group, or race. One of the causes among others is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and trafficking in persons that has occurred so far is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and the Indonesian Child Prevention Network (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, the Regional Government also has the obligation and responsibility to prevent and sanction acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, healing and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus it is expected that the main objective of the preparation of this Draft Regional Regulation can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal basis for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons and to ensure the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and combating violence and trafficking.

Article 19

2. The membership of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of related SKPDs, law enforcers, community institutions, universities, and civil society.
3. The formation of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent's Decree.

3. 4. The implementation as referred to in paragraph (3) is in the form of: policy analysis, coordination, advocacy, socialization, communication, information and education (KIE), training, service facilitation, service provision, development of women and child protection models and other forms.

Article 9

a. Preventive or prevention method; and
b. Repressive or handling method.
2. The preventive or prevention method is carried out through various forms of protection, both by the community and the government, which are intended to prevent the occurrence of criminal acts of trafficking in persons and violence or victims of violence against women and children.
3. The repressive or handling method is carried out through various forms of protection carried out by the government through regulatory activities, implementation and enforcement of laws and regulations governing the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons.
4. Guidelines and Technical Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons are further regulated through Regent Regulation.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency. 5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within a country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Rights of the child are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or to a person's body, miscarriage and fainting and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers working abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery. 15. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and obscenity. 17. Recruitment is an act that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community. 18. Transfer is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. Debt bondage is the act of placing a person in the status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people under their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment. 20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination. 22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred. 23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process. 27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved. 29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance. 32. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter referred to as SPO is a procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree. 33.

One of the causes among others is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and trafficking in persons that has occurred so far is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and the Indonesian Child Prevention Network (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, the Regional Government also has the obligation and responsibility to prevent and sanction acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, healing and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus it is expected that the main objective of the preparation of this Draft Regional Regulation can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal basis for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons and to ensure the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and combating violence and trafficking.

Discrimination against women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women; 34. CHAPTER VII

IMPLEMENTATION

Article 18

1. The Regent implements policies, programs, and activities to eliminate all forms of discrimination and acts of violence against women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons.
2. The implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) is coordinated by the Vice Regent.
3. The Office of Women's Empowerment and Family Planning or the SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection together with P2TP2A implements the policies, programs and activities that have been established, and in its implementation cooperates with related SKPDs, law enforcers, community institutions, universities, and civil society.
4. The implementation as referred to in paragraph (3) is in the form of: policy analysis, coordination, advocacy, socialization, communication, information and education (KIE), training, service facilitation, service provision, development of women and child protection models and other forms.

Article 22

1. Facilitation and provision of services as referred to in Article 21 letter c, are in the form of victim identification, legal aid, medical rehabilitation, psychosocial rehabilitation, social reintegration, repatriation assistance, or other forms.
2. Facilitation and provision of services as referred to in paragraph (1) are provided for women and children victims of violence including victims of trafficking in persons, women and children in conflict-prone and disaster areas, women and child workers, elderly women, women and children with disabilities, women and children victims of sexual exploitation, women heads of households, and women and children in other vulnerable groups.

Article 19

1. The implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons is carried out by forming, developing, strengthening, or utilizing task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions.
2. The membership of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of related SKPDs, law enforcers, community institutions, universities, and civil society.
3. The formation of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent's Decree.

Article 17

1. The integration of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons is incorporated into planning and budget documents which include the Regional Long-Term Development Plan (RPJPD), Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD), Strategic Plan of Regional Work Units (Renstra SKPD), Regional Government Work Plan (RKPD), and Work Plan and Budget of Regional Work Units (RKA-SKPD) and related SKPD RKA.
2. The preparation of planning and budget documents as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be harmonized among related Regional Work Units (SKPD).
3. The SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection together with P2TP2A facilitates the integration of policies, programs, and activities for empowerment, protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons into the preparation of planning and budget documents as set forth in paragraph (1).
4. In carrying out as referred to in paragraph (3), the SKPD in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection together with P2TP2A coordinates with the Regional Development Planning Agency.

Article 25

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons is carried out at the end of each fiscal year.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons are used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women for the following year.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 20

1. In implementing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons, the district government may cooperate with international institutions.
2. Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 9

1. The system for implementing protection for victims of trafficking in persons and violence against women and children is carried out through 2 (two) methods, namely:
a. Preventive or prevention method; and
b. Repressive or handling method.
2. The preventive or prevention method is carried out through various forms of protection, both by the community and the government, which are intended to prevent the occurrence of criminal acts of trafficking in persons and violence or victims of violence against women and children.
3. The repressive or handling method is carried out through various forms of protection carried out by the government through regulatory activities, implementation and enforcement of laws and regulations governing the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons.
4. Guidelines and Technical Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons are further regulated through Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VIII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 24

1. To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons, the District Government conducts monitoring.
2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities that have been established.
3. Monitoring is carried out periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of SKPDs that implement policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons.
4. Monitoring is carried out starting from planning up to the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons for the current year.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency. 5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within a country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Rights of the child are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or to a person's body, miscarriage and fainting and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers working abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery. 15. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and obscenity. 17. Recruitment is an act that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community. 18. Transfer is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. Debt bondage is the act of placing a person in the status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people under their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment. 20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination. 22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred. 23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in an effort to strengthen the victim psychologically. 25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as KPPA is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics. 26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process. 27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved. 29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance. 32. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter referred to as SPO is a procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree. 33.

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 28

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including trafficking in persons has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general in nature, having no relevance to level of education, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and belief, as well as particular ethnicity, ethnic group, or race. One of the causes among others is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and trafficking in persons that has occurred so far is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and the Indonesian Child Prevention Network (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. CHAPTER XIII

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 30

1. In the event that the P2TP2A institution has not yet been established, then all implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons, shall be carried out by KPPA.
2. The P2TP2A institution must be established no later than 1 (one) year from the enactment of this Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER X

FUNDING

Article 27

All funds required for activities related to the protection of women and children victims of violence/trafficking in persons, including their recovery process, shall be charged to the Regional Budget of Banyuwangi Regency, as well as other lawful and non-binding revenues.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including trafficking in persons has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general in nature, having no relevance to level of education, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and belief, as well as particular ethnicity, ethnic group, or race. One of the causes among others is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and trafficking in persons that has occurred so far is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and the Indonesian Child Prevention Network (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, the Regional Government also has the obligation and responsibility to prevent and sanction acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, healing and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus it is expected that the main objective of the preparation of this Draft Regional Regulation can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal basis for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons and to ensure the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and combating violence and trafficking.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Banyuwangi Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in Banyuwangi Regency. 5. Woman is a person of female gender. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within a country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Rights of the child are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, mentally, socially, psychosocially, and sexually. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or to a person's body, miscarriage and fainting and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers working abroad and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of such misery. 15. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits either material or immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and obscenity. 17. Recruitment is an act that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community. 18. Transfer is the act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. Debt bondage is the act of placing a person in the status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people under their responsibility or their personal services as a form of debt repayment. 20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination. 22. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is occurring or has occurred. 23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in an effort to strengthen the victim psychologically. 25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as KPPA is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics. 26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purposes of proof in the judicial process. 27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain a sense of security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's messenger, while their case has not been resolved. 29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with family, or substitute family and community supported by the provision of educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance. 32. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter referred to as SPO is a procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree. 33.

Part One

Protection System

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including trafficking in persons has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general in nature, having no relevance to level of education, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and belief, as well as particular ethnicity, ethnic group, or race. One of the causes among others is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and trafficking in persons that has occurred so far is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases that are recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are many more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to a report by the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and the Indonesian Child Prevention Network (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and have potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, the Regional Government also has the obligation and responsibility to prevent and sanction acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, healing and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus it is expected that the main objective of the preparation of this Draft Regional Regulation can be achieved properly, namely to provide a legal basis for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons and to ensure the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and combating violence and trafficking.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including trafficking in persons has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general in nature, having no relevance to level of education, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and belief, as well as particular ethnicity, ethnic group, or race. One of the causes among others is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

Article 9

a. Preventive or prevention method; and
b. Repressive or handling method.
2. The preventive or prevention method is carried out through various forms of protection, both by the community and the government, which are intended to prevent the occurrence of criminal acts of trafficking in persons and violence or victims of violence against women and children.
3. The repressive or handling method is carried out through various forms of protection carried out by the government through regulatory activities, implementation and enforcement of laws and regulations governing the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons.
4. Guidelines and Technical Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons are further regulated through Regent Regulation.
